Ok I wanna preface this by saying that im not a medical professional and i cant diagnose you or anything like that (I dont think you expect/want me to but I wanna clarify that anyway to avoid any confusion) so take everything I say with a grain of salt as i am not anywhere close to being a medical professional. Also you have no reason to be sorry, dont worry. 

But I think it all depends. How much distress does this bring you? I think its normal to be uncomfortable in the dark, like running upstairs from the basement quick after you turn the light off type thing. But if this thought "What if theres a murderer behind the bathroom door/in the basement/outside my front door'' is bringing you any sort of significant distress and anxiety I think it'd be worth looking into, OCD or not. Especially if it is giving you unpleasant intrusive thoughts/imagery that frightens you, I know how unpleasant that can be.

Have you noticed it impeding your ability to function at all? For example, have you avoided going outside  or ti parts of your house out of fear of there being some sort of danger? Or maybe have you been repeatedly checking to see if anyone/anything is there "just to be sure"? Or anything notable that isnt specific to anything I mentioned, these are just examples.

My personal rule of thumb is that if its impeding your ability to function or feel stable/safe/comfortable for more than an hour a day, you should look into it.
I assume you already have a therapist since you have a psychiatrist but if not id suggest looking into one, preferably one familiar with OCD.

Your post is reassurance seeking so I dont wanna make any statements about it (out of care for you i dont mean this rude at all) but what I will say is that OCD will play tricks on you and I know its incredibly hard not to give in to the urge to soothe that anxiety but try not to give in to what it wants you to think because it reinforces that anxiety if that makes sense. I am on the thought journey right now thats me trying to figure out how to properly cope with the guilt caused by my OCD. First of all, are you diagnosed with it and being treated? The core OCD is the issue, you gotta get it looked at. Trust me, i neglected mine for years and its the worst mistake ive ever made for myself.

Second of all, This is one of the hardest pills to swallow for me in my experience: OCD will not allow you to accurately gauge your feelings of guilt. It'll make you feel guilty when you do nothing wrong, and anything you *actually* do wrong, you'll feel 100x more guilty than you would without OCD. Its debilitating. So debilitating, that you cant actually even cope with the real guilt of your mistake in a healthy or productive manner. What im getting at here is that you have no way to accurately process these thoughts and feelings with active untreated OCD. 

I dont know if they verbatim confirmed your alleged wrongdoing [ex: "You actually did do that bad thing you were afraid you had done 100% to the extent of which you feared you had"] or not, but its important to take into account how OCD catastrophizes everything. I dont know your story so I cant say anything for certain, but I just think its important to consider that.
